description: Refining of tincal/borate ore to refined borax (disodium tetraborate)
source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 - Boron (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2025/mcs2025-boron.pdf); tincal mined and refined into sodium borate at U.S. Borax Boron CA plant

description: Borax + sulfuric acid -> boric acid (+ sodium sulfate)
source: IMFORMED - Rio Tinto Minerals borates production (https://imformed.com/rio-tinto-minerals-borates-production-up-3/); Boric Acid Plant at Boron CA uses sulfuric acid to dissolve kernite/borax; Na2B4O7+H2SO4+5H2O -> 4H3BO3+Na2SO4

description: Dehydration of boric acid -> boron oxide (B2O3)
source: Wikipedia - Boron trioxide (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boron_trioxide); H3BO3 -> HBO2 -> B2O3 by controlled heating; note both compounds share HS 281000 so this route only counts under lenient matching

description: Magnesiothermic reduction of B2O3 -> elemental boron
source: Wikipedia - Boron (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boron); Moissan process reduction of boric oxide with magnesium metal to elemental boron

description: Boric acid + ammonia/urea -> hexagonal boron nitride
source: IntechOpen - Powder Preparation Properties and Industrial Applications of Hexagonal Boron Nitride (https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/42532); industrial nitriding of boric acid/urea under ammonia atmosphere

description: Boron oxide + carbon (carbothermal) -> boron carbide
source: Wikipedia - Boron carbide (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boron_carbide); 2B2O3+7C -> B4C+6CO carbothermal reduction in electric arc furnace. HS code corrected from seed 284920 (silicon carbide) to 284990 (Of boron; confirmed via H6_rollup.md)

description: Boron trifluoride from boric acid/B2O3 + HF
source: Wikipedia - Boron trifluoride (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boron_trifluoride); B2O3+6HF -> 2BF3+3H2O; industrial scale (2300-4500 t/yr)

description: Isotopic enrichment of boron-10 from boric acid
source: IAEA INIS - Enrichment of boron 10 (https://inis.iaea.org/records/9yw27-b7b07); chemical exchange distillation/ion exchange of boric acid is the only industrial-scale B-10 separation method

description: Gallium recovered from Bayer-process sodium aluminate liquor
source: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 - Gallium (https://pubs.usgs.gov/periodicals/mcs2025/mcs2025-gallium.pdf): Bayer liquor feed for gallium recovery is a sodium aluminate solution (450 g/L Na2O, 80 g/L Al2O3, ~190 ppm Ga), i.e. an aluminate salt in solution, not solid aluminium hydroxide. Per H6_rollup.md, 284190 explicitly lists 'Aluminates' (grep -n '^284190' H6_rollup.md); 281830 is 'Aluminium hydroxide' (Al(OH)3), the precipitated PRODUCT of the Bayer process, not the gallium-bearing liquor. Code corrected from seed 281830 to 284190 on chemistry + H6_rollup.md grounds only (MEKH state files not consulted).

description: Gallium + arsenic -> gallium arsenide (single crystal)
source: OSHA - Semiconductors: Gallium Arsenide Ingot Growing (https://www.osha.gov/semiconductors/gallium-arsenide/ingot-growing); elemental Ga and As react at elevated temperature to grow GaAs ingots (LEC/VB/VGF methods). HS code corrected from seed 285000 (nitride/boride bucket) to 285390 (Gallium arsenide wafers; undoped; confirmed via H6_rollup.md)

description: Trimethylgallium from gallium trichloride + methylmagnesium/aluminium
source: Starowieyski et al. Synthesis and purification of trimethylgallium for MOCVD (https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1002/1099-0739(200010)14:10<616::AID-AOC47>3.0.CO;2-T); GaCl3 + Me2AlCl (NaCl catalyst) -> Me3Ga. HS code corrected from seed 293100 (non-existent code) to 293190 (organo-inorganic compounds n.e.c.; confirmed via H6_rollup.md)

description: Gallium nitride via MOCVD from trimethylgallium + ammonia
source: Wikipedia - Gallium nitride, section 'Metal-organic vapour phase epitaxy' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallium_nitride): 'The precursors are ammonia with either trimethylgallium or triethylgallium...Growth temperature ranges between 800 and 1100C.' Directly confirms TMG+NH3 -> GaN by MOCVD. Replaces prior Patsnap aggregator source.

description: Gallium oxide from gallium metal (oxidation/hydroxide calcination)
source: US Patent 4081523A - Method for the production of gallium oxide (https://patents.google.com/patent/US4081523A/en); gallium metal hydrolyzed/oxidized to GaOOH then calcined to Ga2O3

description: Germanium concentrate (zinc residue / fly ash) -> crude GeO2
source: Wikipedia - Germanium (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium); germanium recovered as byproduct from sphalerite zinc ore residues and coal fly ash; converted to germanium dioxide

description: GeO2 + HCl -> germanium tetrachloride
source: Wikipedia - Germanium (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium); GeO2 + 4HCl -> GeCl4 + 2H2O

description: Hydrolysis of purified GeCl4 -> high-purity GeO2
source: Wikipedia - Germanium (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium); GeCl4 purified by fractional distillation then hydrolyzed back to GeO2; note both compounds share HS 282560 so this route only counts under lenient matching

description: Hydrogen reduction of GeO2 -> germanium metal
source: Wikipedia - Germanium (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium); GeO2 + 2H2 -> Ge + 2H2O

description: Zone refining of germanium metal -> electronic-grade germanium
source: Wikipedia - Germanium (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germanium); zone refining reduces impurities to ~1 part in 10^10; note purification step shares HS 811292 so this route only counts under lenient matching

description: Copper-cobalt ore -> cobalt hydroxide via hydrometallurgical leaching and precipitation
source: Fisher, K.G. 2011. Cobalt Processing Developments. Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, 6th Southern African Base Metals Conference (https://www.911metallurgist.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Cobalt-processing-developments.pdf); Sec 3.2 (DRC/Zambian Cu-Co ores): '...sulphuric acid atmospheric leach and direct copper EW; plus impurity removal and cobalt hydroxide precipitation'. Replaces prior MDPI (403, unread) + Britannica (403, unread, non-spec) citations with a source actually fetched and read in full.

description: Cobalt hydroxide + sulfuric acid -> cobalt sulfate
source: Fisher, K.G. 2011. Cobalt Processing Developments. Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, 6th Southern African Base Metals Conference (https://www.911metallurgist.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Cobalt-processing-developments.pdf); Sec 3.2 (DRC/Zambian Cu-Co ores): roast-leach-electrowin flowsheet includes 'cobalt hydroxide precipitation, often followed by re-leach and cobalt EW'; Sec 5.3 lists 'Cobalt sulphate' as a standard cobalt product form. Re-leaching precipitated Co(OH)2 with sulfuric acid to produce the cobalt sulfate feed for electrowinning is the standard next step in this flowsheet.

description: Electrowinning of cobalt sulfate solution -> cobalt cathode metal
source: Fisher, K.G. 2011. Cobalt Processing Developments. Southern African Institute of Mining and Metallurgy, 6th Southern African Base Metals Conference (https://www.911metallurgist.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/02/Cobalt-processing-developments.pdf); Sec 3.2: RLE flowsheet ends in 're-leach and cobalt EW' (electrowinning); Sec 5.3 lists 'Cobalt electrowon cathode - HG (99.8%) or LG (99.3%)' as a standard cobalt product produced from the sulfate electrolyte.

description: Cobalt sulfate + lithium carbonate -> lithium cobalt oxide (calcination)
source: US Patent - Cobalt oxide as a precursor of positive electrode materials for rechargeable lithium-ion batteries (https://patents.google.com/patent/US12227430); cobalt sulfate converted to cobalt oxide/hydroxide precursor; calcined with lithium carbonate to LiCoO2 cathode material
